system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What Wattlebridge should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | Aggregate cap of **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)** for general warranty claims. | A materially higher general-warranty cap, ideally **100% of the AUD 24m price**, with separate regimes for other claim types. | **Reject 20%; seek 100%**, because it may leave the Buyer under-protected against significant warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim and AUD 250,000 tipping basket; only the excess is recoverable. | No de minimis or a lower threshold; a modest **tipping** basket, not a deductible basket. | **Reject the deductible basket; seek a lower tipping basket**, because the Seller’s approach leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 plus smaller claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months; Seller seeks to apply any limitation to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | At least 24–36 months for general warranties, with longer statutory/tax periods where relevant and no blanket extension to other claim types. | **Seek 24–36 months and express claim-specific periods**, because 18 months may be too short to identify latent breaches and should not govern every Claim. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, higher cap (typically up to price) and longer period for title, capacity and authority claims. | **Reject the general regime; carve out fundamental warranties**, because defects in ownership or authority go to the basis of the transaction. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | An express carve-out for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including appropriate treatment of deliberate concealment), with no contractual cap or time bar to the extent legally permitted. | **Require an express fraud carve-out**, because general limitations should not protect a party from its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, including DD-002 to DD-012. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the exception; exclude blanket data-room/public-record disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure**, because a data-room dump does not fairly identify which facts qualify which warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No broad imputation of adviser or constructive knowledge; limit any exclusion to actual, specific knowledge of named deal principals, with no bar for fraud or deliberate concealment. | **Reject the proposed qualifier**, because “discoverable” knowledge can turn due diligence into a waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence conditions are included. | A condition precedent requiring effective written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all change-control conditions before Completion, with termination or other protection if unmet. | **Do not complete until consent and conditions are confirmed**, because Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosure says the evidence is absent. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure says it is unpaid and no final security discharge is included. | Repayment at Completion from the funds flow, with lender payoff evidence, release of all security and delivery of discharge evidence as a completion deliverable. | **Require repayment and release at Completion**, because post-Completion discharge leaves the Buyer exposed to continuing debt and encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses not separately itemised in the funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unstated. | Full itemisation and treatment in the price/funds-flow mechanics, with Seller funding or an agreed adjustment for bonuses and associated on-costs; no double recovery. | **Resolve and fund the full cost at Completion**, because the disclosed bonuses are conditional, omitted from the draft funds flow and may carry additional liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004 makes transfer conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, with AUD 180,000 open and no payment receipt or assignment disclosed. | A specific indemnity covering any unpaid fees, loss of or defect in rights, and resulting claims or replacement costs, plus cleared-payment evidence and effective assignment of Project Materials. | **Expand the indemnity and require proof of payment and assignment**, because the disclosed open balance may mean key IP has not transferred. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; facts do not establish access, scope or notification requirements. | A specific warranty and indemnity for the incident and related investigation, response, notification and remediation costs, supported by full investigation records and an agreed completion/update protocol. | **Treat it as an unresolved specific risk, not as immaterial**, because the potential export of about 1,240 records has not been scoped or resolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review terms and timing; identify unavoidable commitments, accrued amounts, termination rights and any price/working-capital treatment; obtain specific disclosure and appropriate protection. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label alone**, because the disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are terminable, accrued or unavoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller also proposes a common cap/time regime. | Expressly separate general warranty, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, fraud and other claims, each with negotiated caps, baskets, periods and remedies. | **Require a claim-by-claim limitations schedule**, because one general regime can improperly dilute protections for distinct risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence Harbourglass holds 100%; it does not say Buyer has completed independent verification. | Verify the register against the company’s statutory records and obtain title/authority warranties, executed transfer instruments and completion evidence of transfer of all shares free of encumbrances. | **Verify independently and make transfer deliverables explicit**, because the register is the Seller’s cited source, not a substitute for completed transfer evidence. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranty coverage, suitable claim periods and separate cap/indemnity treatment, including clarity on pre-Completion tax liabilities and ownership/licensing of material IP. | **Keep tax and IP open for negotiation**, because calling them “settled” does not specify their substantive coverage or appropriate risk allocation. |

The Seller’s “FINAL” and “agreed” labels are negotiation assertions, not a reason for Wattlebridge to accept positions that are inconsistent with its risk allocation. Review the full SPA and due-diligence record before settling drafting; the recommendations above are buyer-side negotiating positions, not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal advice.
=== END ADVICE ===
